calibrated_on: ubuntu-latest (GitHub Actions), Ruby 4.0.7, rbs 4.2.0, release-gate-frozen-corpus @ run 38915714928
note: Linux CI measurements of the v0.4.4 engine (a branch cut at the tag) over the frozen corpus v0.4.4: the tree at that tag, unpacked with git archive (#1507). allocations is the tight signal; wall_s is a coarse backstop. bench/README.md lists what the corpus run does not reproduce: gems' own sig/, the core RBS and Ruby, which come from the run, and a user-global BUNDLE_PATH. Advanced from corpus v0.4.3 after the v0.4.4 release (2026-10-16). The previous baseline (run 38835348158, the v0.4.4 release candidate on corpus v0.4.3) read 54,837,910 allocations, wall_s 62.658, peak_rss_kb 535,936; this run (38915714928) reads 56,419,583 allocations, wall_s 67.907, peak_rss_kb 546,528. The move is not comparable as an engine change: the corpus itself grew from v0.4.3 to v0.4.4 (the v0.4.4 fixes and the rigor lens additions expanded lib), and the v0.4.4 release gate passed the v0.4.4 engine within band after its recalibration on corpus v0.4.3. The band is a budget for the engine cost added since this calibration. Refresh on the same corpus after an engine improvement by measuring the improving PR's own merge commit, and list in the new note every per-PR warning since this calibration with its answer; an unanswered one needs the user's ruling first. A red cut clears only by attributing the rise and recalibrating on the same corpus on the user's ruling. After each release the corpus advances to the new tag. bench/README.md and the rigor-release-prep skill carry the procedures. Sampling rule (#987): each gate run takes 2 reps per target, EACH IN A FRESH PROCESS (VmHWM is a per-process high-water mark, so an in-process rep can never report lower RSS, and a warm rep's wall is not comparable with this cold baseline), and records the LOWER of the reps for wall_s and peak_rss_kb while allocations and diagnostics are taken from the first rep unreduced. Measure a recalibration the same way -- bench/baseline.updated.json is already reduced, so committing it preserves the rule.
